justifications.r1: 10 cheap two-mana mana rocks and talismans plus Sol Ring accelerate Marchesa onto the battlefield consistently by Turn 3.
justifications.r2: A-tier card flow powered by Skullclamp, Grim Haruspex, Mulldrifter (looped on end steps), Baleful Strix, Deadly Dispute, and Scorn-Blade Berserker.
justifications.a1: Premier A-tier redundancy with 8 free sacrifice outlets, 7 aristocrat drain engines, and deep +1/+1 counter enablers forming resilient loops.
justifications.a2: Achieves engine readiness by Turn 4 via fast mana into Marchesa and immediate +1/+1 counter deployment.
justifications.p1: Critical onset hits by Turn 6 as recurring drain engines (Gray Merchant of Asphodel, Flayer of the Hatebound) or persist loops start threatening lethal life totals.
justifications.p2: A-tier win compactness: closing the game takes just 1 opponent response cycle after onset due to high-damage Gray Merchant loops, Flayer burst damage, and Murderous Redcap infinite combos.
justifications.p3: Modified creatures with counters and open sacrifice outlets on the battlefield clearly telegraph end-step reanimation loops.
justifications.i1: B-tier reactive disruption suite featuring Toxic Deluge, Blasphemous Act, Terminate, Bedevil, Feed the Swarm, An Offer You Can't Refuse, and Arcane Denial.
justifications.i2: B-tier proactive denial anchored by looped Kardur, Doomscourge goad locks, Massacre Wurm sweeping opposing boards, and repeated Puppeteer Clique / Zealous Conscripts theft.
justifications.s1: B-tier plan shielding: Marchesa returns dying creatures with +1/+1 counters at end of turn, backed by Swiftfoot Boots, but vulnerable to exile and pre-counter removal.
justifications.s2: A-tier engine recovery: non-exile sweepers simply trigger end-step returns for all modified creatures, while Living Death provides mass resurrection.
justifications.s3: A-tier independence: the 99 functions autonomously as a threat-stealing Grixis aristocrat beatdown and persist combo engine even without Marchesa.

overview: This deck is a high-synergy Grixis Aristocrats build commanded by Marchesa, the Black Rose. Its strategy revolves around utilizing the dethrone mechanic and +1/+1 counter synergies to establish an unyielding reanimation loop. By ensuring creatures have +1/+1 counters via dethrone attacks, Unspeakable Symbol, or Thran Vigil, Marchesa returns them from the graveyard at the beginning of each end step whenever they die. Free sacrifice outlets like Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, and Goblin Bombardment allow the deck to trigger powerful enters-the-battlefield and death abilities across every player's turn. High-impact payoffs like Gray Merchant of Asphodel, Flayer of the Hatebound, Massacre Wurm, and Kardur, Doomscourge drain life totals, wipe opposing boards, and lock opponents out of attacking. Additionally, the deck can execute infinite damage combos using Murderous Redcap alongside +1/+1 counter buffers. While vulnerable to graveyard hate and exile removal, the deck boasts resilient recovery and compounding resource advantage.

core_strategy: Accelerate in the early turns using 2-mana rocks, establishing a free sacrifice outlet like Viscera Seer or Carrion Feeder and a value creature.
Deploy Marchesa, the Black Rose and place +1/+1 counters on your creatures via dethrone combat, Unspeakable Symbol, or Madame Null, Power Broker.
Sacrifice your modified creatures on each player's turn to trigger death and enters-the-battlefield abilities, returning them at every end step.
Close the game by looping drain engines like Gray Merchant of Asphodel and Flayer of the Hatebound, or assembling a Murderous Redcap persist loop.

keep: Hands with 3 lands, at least one 2-mana ramp piece, a cheap sacrifice outlet, and an early card advantage or counter-enabling creature.
avoid: Hands with only high-CMC payoffs (5+ mana), missing black/blue/red color fixing, or hands with no sacrifice outlets and no card draw.

key_tips: Manage your life total carefully; you often want to remain below the highest life total opponent to guarantee dethrone triggers on attack.
Cast Threaten spells like Mark of Mutiny or Zealous Conscripts, put a +1/+1 counter on the stolen creature, and sacrifice it so it returns permanently under your control.
Use Unspeakable Symbol at instant speed to put +1/+1 counters on creatures in response to removal or sweepers, ensuring they recur at the next end step.

critical: Graveyard hate (such as Rest in Peace or Leyline of the Void) permanently disables Marchesa's reanimation trigger and aristocrat payoffs.
Exile-based board wipes (such as Farewell) bypass death triggers entirely, stripping all board presence without recursion.
moderate: Removal targeting Marchesa, the Black Rose immediately upon entry before she gains a +1/+1 counter delays the entire engine.
Thin stack interaction makes the deck vulnerable to fast instant-speed noncreature combo wins.
minor: Life-loss costs from Unspeakable Symbol, pain lands, and Talismans can become dangerous if opponents apply aggressive combat pressure.
